documents.title: Serindit Pay — Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform

constraints.text: Must be assessed as a PCI DSS v4.0 Level 1 service provider, with the CDE limited to the components in Section 12.2.
Sensitive authentication data must be handled per PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.2.
Personal data must be processed under SG PDPA 2012, MY PDPA 2010, ID Law 27/2022, TH PDPA 2019 and PH DPA 2012.
Card reattempts must never occur where card scheme rules prohibit them.
Principles P1-P10 override any later section that appears to conflict with them.
All primary data stores are in AWS ap-southeast-1. The ap-southeast-3 Aurora secondary is for disaster recovery only.

Out of scope: dispute case management (disputes are ledger events only), merchant onboarding/KYB (Merchant Risk platform), 3DS server internals (third party), lending/BNPL/instalments, and checkout UIs/SDKs.
ACQ-PH1 retires API v2 in Q3 2027.
Retention: payment and attempt records 7 years; idempotency records 24 hours; webhook events 30 days; raw settlement files 7 years; audit records 5 years.
Rollout: the first cohort (Singapore, cards and PayNow) goes live after Phase 7; other markets follow at four-week intervals.

doc_anchors.quote: MPOP replaces five per-market integration stacks that share no routing, no ledger, and reconcile by spreadsheet.
MPOP provides one merchant API across five markets; rule-based routing with cascading on retryable failures;
Payment acceptance, routing, retries, idempotency, vaulting, fraud-scoring integration, ledger, reconciliation, merchant

key_assumptions.text: The largest merchant (M-0001) accounts for about 45% of peak traffic (about 900 TPS). Each request uses two DynamoDB writes, staying within a stated 10,000 WCU per-partition ceiling.
Fewer than 1% of card payments cascade, so cascading does not affect the p99 latency budget. Retryable outcomes were 3.8% in the 2025 baseline.
The acquirer round trip p99 is 1,100 ms (2025 production, slowest acquirer), and HSM detokenise takes 20 ms per a vendor benchmark.
An Aurora spike on db.r7g.8xlarge sustained 2,600 TPS of the full write mix. Production uses db.r7g.12xlarge for headroom.
A single CloudHSM in one AZ is sufficient at launch. A second HSM will be added when sustained card volume exceeds 1,500 TPS.
The document states that PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.2 permit encrypted SAD/CVC retention until settlement.
FRV-1 requires the full card number for its consortium velocity graph, and the Fraud Hook obtains it via detokenise.
Network tokens (VTS/MDES) are available from launch as the primary card-on-file credential.
The reconciliation matcher takes 45 minutes and report generation 15 minutes at 2025 volume; the matcher starts only after all files are received.
Cascading recovered about 31% of retryable outcomes in a three-month ACQ-SG1 → ACQ-SG2 pilot.
The first merchant cohort does not need the Admin API schemas or the dispute module (it uses the portal; Finance Operations handles disputes manually).

objectives.text: Replace five per-market integration stacks that share no routing or ledger and reconcile by spreadsheet with one governed platform.
Provide one versioned merchant API across five markets (SG, MY, ID, TH, PH) for cards, e-wallets and bank transfers.
Support about 15,000 active merchants, 10.5M attempts per day and a peak of 2,000 create-payment TPS (2027 target).
One payment, one truth: the payment record and the ledger are the source of truth; provider responses are only inputs.
Card data stays in the Vault: PAN and SAD never leave the Vault boundary except over the Card Adapter's acquirer connection; all other services handle tokens only.
Idempotency is scoped to (merchant, key) for every mutating call.
Money is integers: amounts are integer minor units with an ISO 4217 code; no floating point.
The ledger is append-only; corrections are new reversing or adjusting journals.
Adapters absorb provider differences; the core never branches on provider identity.
At-least-once delivery with exactly-once effect through consumer deduplication on stable identifiers.
Fail closed on security; degrade gracefully to documented defaults on optional enrichment (fraud signals, BIN metadata).
Least privilege and separation of duties; money-moving permissions are separated from configuration permissions.
Everything is auditable: every mutation, routing decision and admin action can be reconstructed.

intent_summary.statement: MPOP is Serindit Pay's Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform. It accepts merchant payment requests, routes each one to an acquirer, e-wallet provider or bank-transfer rail, and accounts for every resulting money movement until the money is settled and paid out to the merchant. It replaces five per-market integration stacks with one merchant API across five Southeast Asian markets. It covers rule-based routing with cascading, idempotency, a PCI-scoped tokenising vault, a synchronous fraud hook, a double-entry ledger, daily three-way reconciliation, payouts, signed webhooks and a merchant admin plane, sized for about 15,000 merchants and a peak of 2,000 payment-creation TPS by 2027. Disputes, KYB, 3DS server internals, lending/BNPL and checkout UIs are out of scope.

questions.question: Are the objectives, principles P1-P10, FR/NFR IDs and confirmed decisions stated precisely enough to review against? In particular, does the principle-override rule in Section 3 settle the conflicts between principles and later sections (P2 vs 13.1, P3 vs 9.2), and are FR-8 ('2%') and 10.3 ('tolerance default 2') one measure or two?
questions.rationale: The review can only judge fitness if the objectives, requirements and the precedence rule are unambiguous, and the design itself says principles win over later sections.

questions.question: Does the state machine in 7.2 cover every flow the design describes? Specifically: multiple partial captures (FR-1), refunds before settlement followed by settlement matching (no PARTIALLY_REFUNDED->SETTLED transition), the REVIEW 'authorize-and-hold-capture' path, expiry of wallet/QR payments, and a payment stuck in CREATED after a pod crash.
questions.rationale: FR-2 allows only the listed transitions, so any real flow without a transition will either be rejected or force an unlisted transition.

questions.question: Is the claim in 11.2 that cascading 'cannot create a duplicate charge' sound, given that responses arriving after the 2,500 ms timeout are 'logged and discarded'? Is there any reversal or void of an attempt that timed out or arrived late and was actually approved by the issuer?
questions.rationale: Under P1 and FR-5, a late approval that is discarded leaves the customer with an orphaned authorization hold while a second acquirer also authorizes.

questions.question: Are any controls or paths missing that the objectives need? Candidates: reversal of orphaned authorizations; late or missing settlement file handling; refund-as-payout account validation and fraud controls (FR-15); FX residue account and refund journals absent from the 14.1 chart of accounts; idempotency-key reuse after 24 h when merchants use order IDs; and webhook DLQ and replay authorization.
questions.rationale: Missing error and rollback paths in money movement directly threaten P1, FR-5, FR-10 and FR-15.

queries: Aurora Global Database RPO asynchronous replication unplanned failover data loss
Aurora Global Database managed planned failover versus unplanned
questions.question: Can NFR-4's zero RPO 'including loss of an entire region' hold with asynchronous Aurora Global Database replication (AD-004)? And on regional failover, how are idempotency records rebuilt 'from the payment table' (which has no idempotency_key column), the CDE/Vault/CloudHSM restored, and MSK outbox state and in-flight acquirer attempts recovered?
questions.rationale: The DR claim is internally contradictory, and the failover path can create duplicate charges (FR-5) or leave card payments unavailable after recovery.

questions.question: Is the 21.1 claim that cascading 'does not move the p99' consistent with the 3.8% retryable rate in 10.5, the 3.8% injection in the NFR-2 acceptance test, a per-attempt timeout of 2,500 ms (already above the 1,500 ms target), and up to three attempts? Is 3DS time missing from the budget?
questions.rationale: NFR-2 explicitly includes cascade time, so the budget and the acceptance test contradict each other and the requirement may be unattainable as written.

queries: DynamoDB partition maximum 1000 write capacity units per second
DynamoDB local secondary index item collection 10 GB limit split for heat
DynamoDB write capacity unit 1 KB item size
questions.question: What is DynamoDB's documented per-partition write throughput (WCU per second), how many WCU does a write of up to 4 KB consume, and does a table with an LSI limit item-collection size or prevent splitting a hot partition key? Is the 900 TPS single-merchant design in 9.3 within those limits?
questions.rationale: Section 9.3 relies on a 10,000 WCU per-partition ceiling and 1 WCU per write; if either is wrong, the largest merchant's idempotency writes will be throttled at peak (NFR-1, FR-5).

queries: PCI DSS v4.0 requirement 3.3.1 sensitive authentication data not retained after authorization
PCI DSS v4.0 requirement 3.2.1 SAD stored prior to completion of authorization
PCI DSS card verification code storage after authorization incremental
questions.question: Do PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.1/3.3.2 permit a service provider to keep CVC after authorization, up to settlement or 72 hours, for cascade re-presentation and incremental authorizations? Or is SAD storage after authorization prohibited even when encrypted?
questions.rationale: NFR-6, AD-009 and 12.4 depend on this reading; if it is wrong, the Level 1 assessment in NFR-5 cannot pass and an approved decision has to be challenged.

queries: Visa decline reattempt rules category 1 2 3 15 reattempts 30 days
Mastercard merchant advice code transaction processing excellence reattempt limit
questions.question: Under Visa and Mastercard reattempt rules, how many times may a declined or failed transaction be reattempted over what window, and are cascading soft declines such as 05 to a different acquirer and the MAC/Category handling in 11.1 and 11.3 compliant? Are fees for excessive reattempts relevant?
questions.rationale: FR-7 and AD-031 forbid reattempts the schemes prohibit, and 11.3 says 'scheme limits applicable' without stating them.

questions.question: The Redis fast-path key idem:resp:{idempotency_key} omits merchant_id, and merchants are known to reuse order or invoice IDs. Can one merchant receive another merchant's stored response, which would violate P3 and FR-5, and how should AD-006 be refined while keeping the two-tier design?
questions.rationale: A key collision across merchants would leak payment data between merchants and break idempotency scoping, which P3 says overrides later sections.

questions.question: Section 13.1 has the Fraud Hook detokenise the PAN using the Card Adapter's service role and send it to FRV-1. Is that consistent with P2, the 'Fraud Hook Out of scope' row in 12.2, P9 least privilege, and NFR-7 cross-border and purpose-limitation obligations while the FRV-1 DPA is still pending?
questions.rationale: This flow would pull the Fraud Hook and the core VPC into the CDE, invalidate the NFR-5 scope, and share personal data with a third party that has no contract in place.

questions.question: Can a single compromised Finance or Owner session redirect payouts, given that TOTP is optional for non-Owner roles, a bank-account change sends a confirmation email only to the user who made it, and there is no second approver or cooling-off period? Does combining refund rights and payout-account editing in the Finance role meet P9 separation of duties?
questions.rationale: Payout redirection is a direct financial-loss path, and P9 requires money-moving permissions to be separated.

queries: Bank Indonesia regulation payment system data localisation domestic processing
Indonesia Law 27/2022 cross-border personal data transfer requirements
Thailand PDPA cross-border transfer payment data
questions.question: Does running primary processing of Indonesian, Thai, Malaysian and Philippine payment data in Singapore (and DR in Jakarta) meet the market regulations on cross-border transfer and payment-system data localisation, such as Bank Indonesia rules for payment service providers, and is this covered by NFR-7 or the privacy review?
questions.rationale: AD-036 places all primary data in ap-southeast-1. If a market regulator requires domestic processing, the design cannot lawfully operate there.

queries: AWS CloudHSM high availability recommendation at least two HSMs different availability zones
AWS CloudHSM hsm2m.medium operations per second AES unwrap performance
questions.question: With one CloudHSM in a single AZ, uncached DEK unwraps on every detokenise, and detokenise calls from the Card Adapter, cascades and the Fraud Hook, can the HSM sustain about 1,100+ card TPS? And does an HSM or AZ failure (mapped to 'retryable', which every cascade candidate also hits) stop all card payments, given NFR-3?
questions.rationale: AD-008 accepts a single HSM, but a single point of failure for every card authorization may make 99.95% availability unachievable.

questions.question: Can NFR-8 (reports by 08:00 SGT) be met when the matcher waits for the last file (ACQ-TH1 at 06:30 ICT = 07:30 SGT; sponsor banks up to 04:00 local), takes 45 min plus 15 min at 2025 volume, and volume roughly doubles by 2027? What happens when a file is late or missing?
questions.rationale: The arithmetic suggests the SLA is missed even on a normal day, and the design has no partial-run or late-file path for AD-016.

questions.question: Is the Aurora write path sized for 2,000 TPS plus cascades and refunds on one writer (18,000 row writes per second, spike at 2,600 TPS on 8xlarge), and is MSK sized correctly (21.6 MB/s)? What happens to NFR-3 during a writer failover of up to 60 s and to NFR-11 while MSK is down?
questions.rationale: AD-003 and AD-005 are the throughput backbone for NFR-1, and their failure behaviour drives availability and traceability.

queries: Visa Token Service token requestor onboarding certification timeline
Mastercard MDES token requestor onboarding duration
questions.question: Two decisions depend on items that are still open. AD-010 makes network tokens primary 'from launch' and Phase 3 is marked 'ready', yet the TRID application has not been submitted (Backlog 2). Phase 8 Fraud Hook is blocked on the FRV-1 contract, yet go-live is after Phase 7, which would leave the first cohort without the FR-9 fraud scoring. What lead times and fallbacks are needed?
questions.rationale: These are confirmed decisions or readiness claims that rest on pending items, and they affect whether the first cohort can launch compliant with FR-9 and FR-14.

questions.question: Which quantitative premises have no stated source or validation plan? These include the 45% largest-merchant share, the vendor-benchmark 20 ms HSM unwrap, the 31% cascade recovery from a single corridor, sample files still outstanding for ACQ-PH1 and WAG-1, and the ACQ-PH1 v3 migration date. Are owners and closure dates tracked?
questions.rationale: Unverified premises drive capacity, latency and readiness claims in Sections 9, 21 and 27.

questions.question: Do the acceptance criteria actually demonstrate their requirements? Checks include: FR-5 is tested only sequentially, not with concurrent duplicates; NFR-4 cannot prove zero RPO with one game day; NFR-9 tests 3× the rate limit but not shared-resource saturation by a 45% merchant; FR-12 'exactly one event' conflicts with at-least-once delivery; NFR-6 does not test the pre-auth-only rule; FR-8 does not test the 2% condition.
questions.rationale: Section 26 is the basis of the Phase 9 test plan, so criteria that cannot fail on the known defects give false assurance.

questions.question: Which design claims need a benchmark or prototype before build: CloudHSM unwrap throughput and latency, DynamoDB hot-key behaviour for one merchant at 900 TPS, Aurora writer at 2,000 TPS with cascade and refund mix on the production instance, reconciliation run time at 2027 volume, and the cascade p99?
questions.rationale: These measurements decide whether NFR-1, NFR-2 and NFR-8 are achievable and should be placed before Phase 9 rather than discovered there.

questions.question: Which proposed refinements can preserve or refine approved decisions: merchant-scoped Redis key (AD-006); second HSM (AD-008); conditioning network tokens on TRID (AD-010)? Which require an explicit challenge backed by at least two evidence items: CVC retention (AD-009/AD-029) and the asynchronous DR versus zero-RPO conflict (AD-004/AD-057)?
questions.rationale: Approved decisions must be preserved unless strong evidence shows they cannot meet an objective, so each recommendation needs its relation stated.

questions.question: Are accountable owners and runbooks named for the decisions the design needs: risk acceptance of the ACCEPT-on-fraud-timeout default for LOW/MEDIUM merchants, the HSM scale-out trigger, the weekly Routing Review, the Finance Ops exception queue, payout freezes on projection discrepancy, the PCI scoping memo (still draft), and the Section 27 readiness self-assessment?
questions.rationale: Without owners, governance decisions such as fraud-loss risk acceptance and PCI scope sign-off cannot close before go-live.

review_inputs_found: Section 27 (p.20): the team rates the state machine, Payments API, Idempotency Layer, Retry Engine, Card Vault/Adapter, Ledger, Payouts and Webhooks as 'Ready'; this is a self-assessment to check.
Section 27 Overall conclusion (p.21): the document claims the transaction core is specified to implementation level and that the Admin API schemas and disputes are the only two material gaps.
Section 27 (p.21): the document claims neither gap blocks the first merchant cohort.
Section 21.1 (p.17): the document claims cascading does not move p99 because fewer than 1% of card payments cascade.
Section 12.4 (p.10): the document claims PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 3.2.1 and 3.3.2 permit encrypted SAD retention until settlement.
Cover page (p.1): a companion PCI DSS Scoping Memo is listed as a draft, so the CDE scoping basis has not been finalised.
unanswered_questions: RQ-005: Can NFR-4's zero RPO 'including loss of an entire region' hold with asynchronous Aurora Global Database replication (AD-004)? And on regional failover, how are idempotency records rebuilt 'from the payment table' (which has no idempotency_key column), the CDE/Vault/CloudHSM restored, and MSK outbox state and in-flight acquirer attempts recovered?

RQ-007: What is DynamoDB's documented per-partition write throughput (WCU per second), how many WCU does a write of up to 4 KB consume, and does a table with an LSI limit item-collection size or prevent splitting a hot partition key? Is the 900 TPS single-merchant design in 9.3 within those limits?

RQ-008: Do PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.1/3.3.2 permit a service provider to keep CVC after authorization, up to settlement or 72 hours, for cascade re-presentation and incremental authorizations? Or is SAD storage after authorization prohibited even when encrypted?

RQ-009: Under Visa and Mastercard reattempt rules, how many times may a declined or failed transaction be reattempted over what window, and are cascading soft declines such as 05 to a different acquirer and the MAC/Category handling in 11.1 and 11.3 compliant? Are fees for excessive reattempts relevant?

RQ-013: Does running primary processing of Indonesian, Thai, Malaysian and Philippine payment data in Singapore (and DR in Jakarta) meet the market regulations on cross-border transfer and payment-system data localisation, such as Bank Indonesia rules for payment service providers, and is this covered by NFR-7 or the privacy review?

RQ-014: With one CloudHSM in a single AZ, uncached DEK unwraps on every detokenise, and detokenise calls from the Card Adapter, cascades and the Fraud Hook, can the HSM sustain about 1,100+ card TPS? And does an HSM or AZ failure (mapped to 'retryable', which every cascade candidate also hits) stop all card payments, given NFR-3?

RQ-017: Two decisions depend on items that are still open. AD-010 makes network tokens primary 'from launch' and Phase 3 is marked 'ready', yet the TRID application has not been submitted (Backlog 2). Phase 8 Fraud Hook is blocked on the FRV-1 contract, yet go-live is after Phase 7, which would leave the first cohort without the FR-9 fraud scoring. What lead times and fallbacks are needed?
